sections.title: Hezekiah's Illness and Prayer
observations: This section describes King Hezekiah's serious illness, which was perceived as a terminal condition. Hezekiah's response to the news of his impending death was one of deep distress, leading him to turn to God in prayer. His prayer is notable for its sincerity and humility, as he reminds God of his faithfulness and good deeds. This highlights the importance of prayer in times of crisis and the personal relationship one can have with God.

sections.title: God's Response and Promise of Healing
observations: God hears Hezekiah's prayer and sends the prophet Isaiah back to deliver a message of healing. This moment emphasizes God's mercy and willingness to respond to the cries of His people. The promise of an additional fifteen years to Hezekiah's life serves as a reminder of God's sovereignty over life and death, and His ability to change circumstances according to His will.

sections.title: The Sign of Healing
observations: To confirm His promise, God provides a miraculous sign: the shadow on the sundial moving backward. This sign serves to strengthen Hezekiah's faith and demonstrates God's power over nature. It also serves as a public affirmation of God's promise, encouraging the people of Judah to trust in God's deliverance.

sections.title: Hezekiah's Song of Thanksgiving
observations: After his healing, Hezekiah composes a song of thanksgiving, reflecting on his experience of suffering and restoration. This song reveals his deep gratitude and recognition of God's faithfulness. It also serves as a theological reflection on life, death, and the hope of resurrection, emphasizing the importance of worship and gratitude in the life of a believer.

importantVerses.commentary: God's promise to add fifteen years to Hezekiah's life illustrates His mercy and willingness to intervene in human affairs.
Hezekiah's acknowledgment of God's deliverance and the importance of gratitude highlights the believer's response to God's grace.

questions: What does Hezekiah's prayer teach us about approaching God in times of distress?
How does God's response to Hezekiah's prayer reflect His character?
What significance does the sign of the sundial moving backward hold for our understanding of God's power?
In what ways can we express gratitude to God for His interventions in our lives?
